expected.meetingPurpose: Review T761 Eakin software coding changes and related technical-file dependencies for alarms, languages, versioning, electrical safety and cybersecurity.
meetingObjectives: Review completed alarm sound, colour and flash changes.
Confirm remaining mute-button and clinical-review actions.
Confirm electrical compliance testing approach and timeline.
Review cybersecurity risks and mitigation options.
expected.executiveSummary: The meeting reviewed software changes for the Eakin technical file, with alarm changes largely completed and language changes underway. Remaining work included mute-button behaviour, clinical review, debug testing, traceability for the 17 historic software changes, and possible retrospective test data. Electrical compliance testing will be completed in-house, while cybersecurity discussion focused on USB-port and GUI controls, including whether physical locks, software controls or benefit-risk rationale are appropriate.
discussion: Andrew has implemented and demonstrated alarm sound changes for low, medium and high priority alarms.
Low, medium and high priority alarm visuals have been updated with colour and LED flash behaviour.
The remaining alarm question is what happens to the LED flashing behaviour when the mute button is pressed.
A clinician mini-review of the audible alarm changes has been pushed to next week because clinical staff are unavailable.
Feedback from clinicians and Adil may determine whether a longer-term usability update is needed.
David wants to confirm which debug commands are physically visible or effective before test scripts are written.
The software change request has been submitted and is expected to be reviewed on Wednesday.
The change request covers alarm code changes, language changes and the retrospective software version change from 1.01 to 1.02.
A further software release will be needed after the change request work is complete.
The change is expected to be treated as non-significant or non-substantial through the regulatory process.
The 17 historic software changes from version 1.01 to 1.02 need a gap assessment to confirm what changed and whether they are visible in code.
If the 17 changes are not all battery-related, additional explanation or retrospective test data may be needed for traceability.
Electrical compliance testing is being brought in-house and is expected to complete by around 23 July in the conservative timeline.
Andrew has started reviewing the 60601-1 compliance document and identifying possible test gaps.
The additional language work can load 18 language files, but Arabic, Vietnamese and Greek may require character or font support.
Cybersecurity and risk discussion covered USB port access, screen access, unauthorised interference, therapy-mode changes and whether a lock, password or benefit-risk rationale is appropriate.
Password protection may introduce clinical usability risk if clinicians need to intervene quickly.
Risk scoring for third-party interference may have high severity in neonatal scenarios but low occurrence based on field experience.
Rebecca is updating the risk management file and has purchased standards that may inform cybersecurity and nebuliser-port assessment.
Fan logic and PMS/risk-management plan updates were also reviewed as part of the technical-file follow-up.
